issues.legal_issue: The appellate court hearing an appeal under Section 37 of the Arbitration and Conciliation Act has a narrower scope of review than the court hearing a challenge under Section 34 and must determine whether the Section 34 court exercised its jurisdiction within the statutory limits.
An appellate court hearing an appeal under Section 37 may remand a Section 34 proceeding only in exceptional circumstances where remand is unavoidable.

A remand was unwarranted where the Section 34 court had already considered the merits of the challenge to the arbitral award in detail, and the Section 37 court should decide the appeal on its merits.
